newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends mixed after long bond volatility.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends mixed after long bond volatility.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed mixed against the dollar after a rollercoaster session due to long bond volatility and swap trades ahead of a forthcoming long weekend, traders said on Thursday.
"Interest rates are attractive option for the investor given the long weekend holiday in the United States," one dealer said.
The 24-hour interbank peso contract ended 0.5 of a centavo firmer at 7.8520/7.8540, while the benchmark 48-hour contract closed 0.5 of a centavo weaker at 7.8640/7.8660.
The 48-hour dollar contract will expire on Tuesday due to Monday's Memorial Day U.S. market holiday.
Traders attributed the market turbulence to a rebound in the U.S.long bond, which was yielding 6.99 percent in late trade after reaching a high during the morning of 7.0 percent.
"There was a little volatility because the bond has been somewhat negative," another dealer added.
The same-day pesos ended earlier unchanged from Wednesday's close of 7.8550/7.8590.
